title: I Used the Seed-Library Checkout on the Chair Who Took the Rare Packets

parts.text: I opened the seed drawer at 11:02 a.m. and the rare tomato packets were gone with the chair's initials in pencil, not the stamp. The card said: STAMP OUT. THREE PACKETS. RARE TO THE QUEUE. Chair Elise palmed two more into a purse. I was thirty-nine, borrower, holding a queue number. "Chairs are the library." I photographed the pencil, the card, and the purse. Then I logged a rare skip. At 11:09 the librarian asked why Elise's pencil was on unstamped rares. I waited where the camera already was. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The librarian can see Elise's pencil initials on unstamped rare packets.

social.video_title: The chair penciled out rares instead of stamping — Part 1/2
social.description: Seed library, a queue number, and a card the chair wrote. I logged the skip. Would you have photographed the purse?

parts.text: Elise called it saving until the librarian asked for the log. I printed the skip, the photo, and the card. Packets went back to the drawer. Elise stamped three and told the queue saving was always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when a pencil exists. Checkout now has a second line: CHAIRS STAMP. I keep my three. Elise waits. The drawer finally looks like a library, not a purse. I go back to being a person with a receipt. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.

social.description: Skip log, returned packets, and a second line. Was saving ever a purse?
